entries.example: We say 'Come in!' when someone knocks at the door of a room.
Then the person who knocked comes into the room.

entries.def: Come out is often the opposite of come in.
entries.example: A woman came out of the shop with two big bags. (I was in the street.)
You put your money in and the ticket comes out of the machine.
She went away for three days. She came back yesterday. (She is here again.)

entries.def: Come back is often used with from.
entries.example: They came back from Italy yesterday.

entries.def: is similar; 'home' is 'here' for the person speaking.
entries.example: MOTHER: What time did you come home last night?
A: What country do you come from?
We're going to a disco tonight. Do you want to come along?
Come and see me some time.
